newsItems.title: Urlando breaks the 200 fly American Record
newsItems.body: Luca Urlando won the 200 butterfly at the U.S. SCM World Championship Trials in Westmont and came away with a new American Record. He described the moment simply: "The energy took over." Worth savoring.

newsItems.title: 89°F pool water at the Youth Olympics
newsItems.body: Pool temperatures in Dakar, Senegal have been measuring above 32°C (89°F) during the 2026 Youth Olympic Games -- at times warmer than the air outside. That is not a training pool in July; that is a hot tub at a competition.

newsItems.title: MSU's new 10-lane 50-meter pool is almost ready
newsItems.body: Michigan State University is putting the finishing touches on a brand-new 10-lane, 50-meter by 25-yard pool with two removable bulkheads and a pair of video boards. New facilities like this matter for the long-term health of the sport in the US.

newsItems.title: Seven countries still chasing the 2036 Olympics
newsItems.body: The IOC has confirmed seven countries remain in the running for the 2036 Summer Olympic Games and the process is now moving into a continuous dialogue phase. Of the seven, only Germany has previously hosted the Summer Games -- back in 1936.

athlete.name: Adam Peaty
athlete.photoCredit: Photo: Fernando Frazão/Agência Brasil, CC BY 3.0 br, via Wikimedia Commons
athlete.bio:
Adam George Ramsay-Peaty is an English competitive swimmer born on 28 December 1994 in Uttoxeter, Staffordshire. He specialises in sprint breaststroke events and did not take swimming seriously until age 17, when he committed fully to the sport after learning a fellow junior swimmer had reached the Olympic semi-finals.

Ramsay-Peaty won gold in the 100 metre breaststroke at both the 2016 and 2020 Summer Olympics, becoming the first British swimmer to retain an Olympic title. He is an eight-time World Champion, sixteen-time European Champion, and four-time Commonwealth Champion. He holds world records in the 50 and 100 metre breaststroke and has broken 14 world records in total.
